question: Does a standard radiance-to-glTF transfer account for appearance loss beyond the audited car, without changing geometry or model inference?
experiment_identity: Two new non-car static-export controls; not the separate active car or non-car revision experiment.
selection_before_outputs: First a smooth glossy household object, then a layered food object from the pinned TripoSR official examples. Neither output has been viewed. No replacement or seed search.
preprocessing: Unmodified upstream remove_background/resize_foreground, foreground ratio0.85 and gray composite. Record existing RGBA behavior and double-alpha as a separate limitation; no mask correction or preprocessing ablation in these cases.
primary_endpoint: Numerical raster-to-decoder RGB transfer on matched visible surfaces and renderer output, not photographic reconstruction accuracy or artist acceptance.
secondary_endpoint: Native field vs mesh views with matched cameras; object shape and appearance must be kept distinct.
success_interpretation: A standard export fix generalizing to both holds would make implementation/representation-transfer a better explanation than generator paint failure, but is not by itself a novel research contribution.
stop: At most one inference per case; retain every output; no repair, topology change, artist revision task, training or remote car generation. If signal disappears under standard conversion, do not promote a new method from this observation.
